text.text_excerpt: Although I have not stayed in the main B&B located at the above address, I have stayed many times at Banana Courtyard's other properties (they are all owned by Mary and Hugh under the same name). I was more than satisfied with each accommodation. I recommend Banana Courtyard to any of my friends who visit New Orleans and I regret that I didn't stay with them on my most recent visit (hence, the review to make up for it!) What you're getting here is special attention from two very passionate owners. All you need to do is take a look at their website. Then email them. Or call them. Ask them questions. Describe what you're looking for and they will give you something to suit your individual t...

Banana Courtyard obtains most of its business through word of mouth, and it's easy to see why they stay booked, even months in advance. The entrance is unassuming, as with so many buildings in the vicinity of the French Quarter, but past the gate and through the front door it becomes clear that you're in a place as lovely as it is unique. Inside, the building is filled with wall-to-wall books, prints, and other curiosities. Mary and Hugh make every effort to ensure that their guests feel like they're staying at someone's home rather than in a hotel - you can expect to be offered a beverage when you arrive and most reasonable, polite requests will be granted. LOVELY!!!! EVERYTHING about our stay at Banana Courtyard was wonderful! I have to focus so that this review does not turn into a book on the glories of this place. OK, here we go... LOCATION...a very quick walk from the heart of the French Quarter or to Frenchman Street, even after drinking several Hurricanes...but far enough away to ensure a peaceful rest. DECOR... makes you feel like you are in N'Awlins 1920-40. The rooms are studded with antique furniture, knick knacks and art from a bygone era.
